Giza. 1: one pyramid in rough steps with ramps; 2: cased in white limestone with a causeway; 3: three pyramids and the Sphinx
Babylon. 1: a stepped brick terrace; 2: planted terraces with a water screw; 3: the full tiered garden with cascades and cedars
an early rammed-earth wall. 1: a stretch of earth wall; 2: brick-faced with a watchtower; 3: a long crenellated wall with two towers climbing a ridge
Alexandria. 1: a colonnaded hall; 2: a second hall and a garden; 3: the full complex with a domed reading room and statues
Rome. 1: the arena with one storey of arches; 2: three storeys; 3: the full ring with the attic, awnings (team) and the surrounding plaza
Pharos. 1: the square base; 2: the octagonal middle; 3: the round lantern with a fire and a statue, on a mole
Istanbul. 1: one covered street; 2: a cross of covered streets with domes; 3: the whole roofscape of domes, gates and caravanserai
Chartres or Cologne. 1: the nave in scaffolding; 2: the nave and transept with a rose window; 3: twin spires and flying buttresses
Beijing. 1: the Meridian Gate and a courtyard; 2: the Hall of Supreme Harmony on its marble terraces; 3: the full axis of halls inside the moat and wall
Greenwich or Jantar Mantar. 1: an octagonal tower; 2: a dome with a telescope; 3: a second dome, a meridian line and a time ball
Venice. 1: a walled dock with one shed; 2: covered slipways and a rope walk; 3: the great gate with lions, cranes and a ship on the stocks
Versailles. 1: the central block; 2: the two wings; 3: the parterre gardens, fountains and the Grand Canal
Cape Canaveral. 1: a launch pad and a gantry; 2: a vehicle assembly building; 3: a rocket on the pad with a crawler and a control centre
a trading tower (think the Bund or Canary Wharf). 1: a podium hall; 2: a glass tower; 3: twin towers with a sky bridge and a plaza
a reactor site. 1: a lab block; 2: a reactor dome; 3: the dome, two cooling towers and a containment ring

a monastery cloister with a scriptorium wing

a brick mill with a tall chimney and a water wheel or beam engine
a sawtooth-roof factory with two chimneys and a yard
a small stepped shrine with an altar and standards (team)
a peripteral temple on a podium (variant b in the big town: a Chinese temple hall)

a stone quay with a breakwater, a warehouse and two moored boats
slipways with a hull in frame, a crane, a rope walk
a dry dock, a sea wall with cannon, a signal mast

an open pit with ladders, a smelting hearth, ore baskets
a bloomery furnace with bellows and a charcoal pile

Sumerian or New Kingdom Egyptian spearmen: a bronze or leather cap, a large hide or wicker shield, a bronze-tipped spear 2.2 m, a linen kilt, bare feet or sandals, a dagger

an Egyptian or Hittite light chariot: two horses, a driver and an archer, a wicker cab on two six-spoke wheels, 2.2 m long. Draw the chariot, the team and the two crew as separate figures on `pose.png`
Egyptian archers: a self bow 1.5 m, a quiver on the back, a linen kilt, a headcloth, no armour
an Assyrian wheeled ram: a timber frame with a hide roof, a beam with a bronze head, four wheels, about 6 m long and 2.2 m high, with three crew
a two-ox cart with sacks, jars and a tarpaulin, a drover with a staff
Roman legionaries of the Principate: lorica segmentata, a Gallic helmet, a curved rectangular scutum (team colour face), a gladius, a pilum beside the figure
Companion or Roman auxiliary cavalry: a horseman in a muscle cuirass or mail, a Boeotian helmet, a long lance (xyston) 3.5 m, a round shield, a saddle cloth, no stirrups
Scythian or Cretan archers: a composite recurve bow 1.2 m, a gorytos quiver on the hip, a pointed cap, a tunic and trousers
a Roman torsion ballista on a stand, 1.9 m high, two torsion springs, a winch, a bolt, two crew
Roman engineers: a tunic, a dolabra pick, a pack with stakes and a basket, a measuring rod
Swiss or Flemish pikemen of the 1300s: a kettle hat, a padded gambeson or brigandine, a 4.5 m pike held at the slope, a short sword, hose
a mid 1300s knight: a bascinet with a visor, mail and plate, a heater shield (team), a 3.5 m lance with a pennon (team), a caparisoned horse (team cloth)
English longbowmen: a 1.9 m yew bow, arrows pushed through the belt, a padded jack, a kettle hat or a hood, a buckler and a sword
a counterweight trebuchet 4.5 m high with the arm down, a sling, a counterweight box, a timber frame, three crew
medieval pioneers: a hood, a leather apron, a mattock, a wicker gabion, a bundle of fascines
1700s line infantry: a tricorne, a long coat with turnbacks (team colour facings), a flintlock musket 1.5 m with a bayonet, a cartridge box, gaiters
1700s dragoons: a tricorne or a helmet with a crest, a coat (team facings), a carbine on a sling, a sabre, a horse with a saddle roll
1800s riflemen: a shako or a forage cap, a short dark green or grey jacket, a rifle 1.2 m, a powder horn, a sword bayonet
a 12-pounder field gun on a two-wheel carriage with a limber, 1.5 m high, three crew with a rammer and a linstock
1700s sappers: a leather cap, an apron, a pick and shovel, a gabion, a powder keg
present-day infantry: a helmet with cover, a plate carrier and pouches, camouflage (the team colour on a shoulder patch and the helmet band), an assault rifle 0.9 m, boots
a present-day main battle tank: 2.5 m high, about 10 m long with the gun, a turret with a 120 mm gun, tracks, side skirts, a commander's hatch (team colour as a turret stripe)
a two-man anti-tank team: a tripod-mounted guided missile launcher, the gunner kneeling, the loader with a missile tube
a towed 155 mm howitzer in the firing position, 2.6 m high, split trails, a muzzle brake, three crew
a towed twin 35 mm anti-aircraft gun on a four-wheel carriage, with a radar trailer, three crew
a present-day multirole fighter (a generic twin-tail delta or swept wing, no real type), 16 m long, 10 m wingspan, two missiles under the wings, drawn also with the landing gear up

an Egyptian or Minoan war galley: 25 m, one bank of oars, a square sail, a raised fighting platform, a ram
an Athenian trireme: 37 m, three banks of oars, a bronze ram, eyes on the bow, two steering oars
a 1300s cog: 24 m, a single square sail, high fore and stern castles, a stern rudder, clinker planking
a 1790s frigate: 45 m, three masts, a single gun deck with 14 gunports a side, a figurehead
a present-day destroyer: 150 m, a forward 5 inch gun, a vertical launch block, a radar mast, a helicopter deck aft
a Roman corbita: 25 m, a round hull, a square mainsail and a small bow sail (artemon), a swan-neck sternpost, a deckhouse aft
a 1480s carrack: 30 m, three masts, a high stern castle, a lateen mizzen
a 1600s galleon: 45 m, a beakhead, a square tuck stern, two gun decks lightly armed
a present-day landing ship: 120 m, a flat bow with doors and a ramp, a tall bridge aft, a vehicle deck
a Phoenician bireme: 25 m, two banks of oars, a ram, a small sail
a Viking longship: 28 m, one square sail, a dragon prow, shields along the gunwale (team), 16 oars a side
a Baltimore clipper schooner: 30 m, two raked masts, sharp lines, four guns a side
a present-day attack submarine: 100 m, a sail with planes, drawn surfaced
a present-day aircraft carrier: 300 m, an angled deck, an island, four jets on the deck
